items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: I started taking lessons off P.M. Williams.

ctx.x: No. I don't think so, no. So my brother knew I was getting stuck on the drums, and he didn't want me to go that route, because he said, 'One thing, you're not going to get too big' and... We were talking about this last night. The drums in those days were like 28 inches, you know. Sometimes bigger. And carrying all those drums, with the big tom-toms and the cymbals, it would be too much! And you didn't have no band-boys in those days, you know.
So he talked my people into getting me a horn for Christmas. They got me a trumpet. And I started taking lessons off P.M. Williams.
How do you spell that first name?
